correctness.rationale: PASS: A nonempty closed connected subset of the countably infinite metric star either includes the common origin and has a unique endpoint vector in [0,infinity]^N, or is one closed bounded interval/tail in a single arm not containing the origin. By the unique ray paths, Hausdorff distance between origin-containing profiles is exactly sup_i|a_i-b_i| with infinite-coordinate mismatch giving infinite distance. Extended-metric finite-distance equivalence classes are clopen, so cannot be crossed by a connected path. On a common infinite-index set with bounded finite differences, affine interpolation is Hausdorff-Lipschitz; intervals and tails slide to canonical origin-containing profiles. Therefore every clopen class is path-connected, hence is a connected component. Profiles a_i=ri for r in [0,1] give continuum distinct classes and the countable metric star is second-countable, bounding its closed subsets by continuum. No experimental extrapolation involved.
